records.title: Testing Agent Skills Systematically with Evals
records.relevance_note: Official OpenAI writeup tying captured agent traces to deterministic grading.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The post recommends `codex exec --json` so an eval harness can score what actually happened, not only whether the final output looks right.
With `--json`, stdout becomes a JSONL stream of structured events, enabling deterministic checks over behavior such as command execution and ordering.
The writeup explicitly advises grounding evals in behavior by capturing JSONL and checking `command_execution` events.

records.title: Codex exec/CLI "Invalid Responses API request" error with OpenRouter
records.relevance_note: Issue body contains raw `codex exec --json` output with event fields.
records.reason_included: Included for concrete command-receipt and token-usage schema.

claim_snippets.claim_text: A successful exec JSONL trace includes top-level lifecycle events such as `thread.started`, `turn.started`, and item events.
A `command_execution` item in the trace records `command`, `aggregated_output`, `exit_code`, and `status`.
The same trace ends with `turn.completed` carrying `input_tokens`, `cached_input_tokens`, and `output_tokens`.

records.title: feat(exec): emit rate_limits in exec mode JSONL output
records.relevance_note: Issue traces a missing cost-telemetry field from code path to emitted JSONL.
records.reason_included: Included for cost attribution failure and code-path detail.

claim_snippets.claim_text: `codex exec` mode always yields `rate_limits: null` in rollout JSONL and in `TokenCount` events, preventing real-time usage display in tooling.
The issue points to `codex-rs/exec/src/event_processor_with_jsonl_output.rs` and notes the exec path already handles `RateLimitsUpdated`, but `ev.rate_limits` is always `None` at runtime.
The comparison payload shows the expected emitted fields under `rate_limits`, including `primary.used_percent`, `window_minutes`, and `resets_in_seconds`.

records.title: WSL tab close during running turn leaves resumed session stuck in Working (missing task_complete)
records.relevance_note: Resume bug is tied directly to incomplete lifecycle logging in the session file.
records.reason_included: Included for recovery dependence on complete turn receipts.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Closing a still-running WSL terminal tab can leave a reopened `codex resume` session stuck in `Working (...)` forever.
In the affected session file, the last turn contains `task_started` but has no matching `task_complete` and no `turn_aborted`.

records.title: Codex desktop can hang when two long-running tool calls start in parallel in one turn
records.relevance_note: Parallel tool-call failure is documented via missing downstream events in the rollout log.
records.reason_included: Included for silent action-loss observability regression.

claim_snippets.claim_text: When two long-running tool calls start in parallel in the same turn, Codex desktop can lose tool outputs and leave the turn permanently unfinished.
The expected event sequence includes `function_call_output` for each tool call plus a final answer and `task_complete`.
The observed sequence emitted two `function_call` events but no later `function_call_output` for either call and no `task_complete`.

records.title: codex exec resume accepts nonexistent session ids and starts a new thread instead of failing
records.relevance_note: Resume integrity failure is shown with raw JSONL output and exit-code behavior.
records.reason_included: Included for replay and reconstruction integrity failure.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Passing a nonexistent UUID to `codex exec resume` starts a brand-new thread instead of returning a not-found error, and the command exits `0`.
The observed transcript begins with `thread.started` for a different `thread_id` than the UUID supplied to `resume`.
The issue states this behavior makes `resume` unsafe for automation because a typo or stale id can silently create a fresh session.

records.title: Resuming after interrupt doesn't reuse prior task outputs when interrupt is in subgraph
records.relevance_note: Minimal repro shows subgraph resume losing linkage despite explicit checkpointing and thread_id.
records.reason_included: Included for branching and subgraph trace-correlation failure.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The repro uses `InMemorySaver`, `interrupt`, and a shared `thread_id` to test resume semantics across a graph and a parent graph.
With the direct graph structure, resume behaves correctly: the second run continues from the interrupt and does not rerun `step_1`.
When the same flow is wrapped in a parent graph, the output shows duplicated interrupt IDs and reruns `step_1`, so prior task outputs are not reused.

records.title: bug: add_messages(format="langchain-openai") strips message IDs and additional_kwargs
records.relevance_note: Minimal repro shows silent loss of message identity and custom metadata during reducer formatting.

claim_snippets.claim_text: `add_messages(left, right, format="langchain-openai")` returns messages whose `id` fields are `None` instead of preserving the original IDs.
The same reducer path drops custom `additional_kwargs`, returning `{}` instead of the supplied metadata.
The issue states the impact is that reducer calls assign new random UUIDs, breaking ID-based deduplication and update logic while silently losing custom data.

records.title: es617/claude-replay: Convert AI coding agent sessions (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) into self-contained, embeddable HTML replays
records.relevance_note: Repo reconstructs and round-trips multi-tool agent session logs into replay artifacts.
records.reason_included: Included for replay support, combined-session linkage, and data-capture caveats.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The repo converts Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and OpenCode session logs into interactive HTML replays, and documents transcript roots including `~/.codex/sessions/<date>/`.
It supports chaining multiple sessions into one replay and can extract embedded turn data back to JSONL or JSON so the replay can be regenerated.

Replay files embed the full transcript, including source code, file paths, tool inputs or outputs, and thinking traces; hiding turns in the player does not remove the underlying recoverable data blob.

records.relevance_note: Outlines advanced cryptographic methods to ensure trace integrity and WORM compliance for run histories.

AES Scenario Merkle Sync continuously generates cryptographic hashes of the environment state and appends them to a Merkle tree, guaranteeing a Root Verify capability against post-execution alteration.

records.title: Postmortem: Silent Multi-Agent Failure via Context Compression Regression
records.relevance_note: A critical postmortem detailing how invisible permission truncation causes agent capabilities to silently degrade without throwing system errors.
records.reason_included: Direct evidence of failure cases caused by misleading or incomplete contextual observability.

claim_snippets.claim_text: An automated context-compression routine silently deleted 62% of invocation permissions (from 26 lines down to 10), completely dropping bash and npm tool access patterns.

Because the coordinator operated statelessly without cross-session memory, it interpreted blocked invocations as an intrinsic lack of capability rather than a monitorable system error, leading to silent systemic failure.

records.title: History replay broken: JSON.stringify fails on reasoning_content control characters
records.relevance_note: Documents a critical failure where capturing model I/O broke the runtime due to serialization incompatibility.
records.reason_included: Satisfies requirement for issue thread about broken replay and silent state loss.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Models like Qwen 3.5 output reasoning_content containing 0x00 to 0x1F control characters which JSON.stringify failed to properly escape to \uXXXX.
The failure to sanitize the reasoning payload caused upstream Python FastAPI parsers to reject history replays with a '422 Unprocessable Entity' error, entirely breaking multi-turn execution.

records.title: Stateless Context Drops with store: false parameter
records.relevance_note: Demonstrates continuity loss when utilizing specific stateless parameter settings over multiple execution turns.
records.reason_included: Highlights the necessity of replaying full cryptographic objects, not merely ID summaries, to maintain multi-turn trajectory context.

claim_snippets.claim_text: When configured with store: false, the receiving server retained absolutely no persistent memory, requiring the full cryptographic payload of the reasoning block to be manually replayed within the encrypted_content field.
Attempting to replay state using only the ID and summary of a prior reasoning item resulted in a complete breakdown of multi-step logic execution.
